correctness.rationale: For every n≥1 the shift transfers exactly n coordinates across the ℓ2/ℓp junction. The upper bounds are the sharp ℓr^{n+1} to ℓs^{n+1} embedding constants after grouping the untouched tail by its norm; all equality vectors are explicitly finite support. Opposite direction contraction follows ℓp versus ℓ2 monotonicity. Polynomial power bounds yield spectral radii one for U and its inverse; rotational diagonal similarity forces σ(U)=𝕋. Unbounded powers in one direction exclude any equivalent isometric norm, while the ordinary ℓp bilateral shift gives a distinct isometric extension. Computational optimization over six exponents and three powers agreed, but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 Wold extension paper itself identifies that its canonical ℓ2-sum construction need not be unitary. Determining the exact full power-growth invariant answers the motivated stability question: the chosen extension is spectrally unit-circle but has sharp one-direction polynomial instability, in fact not even equivalent-isometrically renormable, despite existence of a genuinely isometric alternative. This is a structural boundary of an explicit model relevant to future use of such extensions in dynamics and operator functional calculus; it is not merely the one-step failure of the norm identity.
